about: INTERIM HOTFIX 2026-10-27 (Strategy ruling): `default` is v1 again, so a page with no ?rules= gets V1's rules and ?rules=m4 opts in: with M4 on by default the evaluator's own torso pool (~76) ran down on light hits (about every 4-7 light hits) and its `kill`/`knockdown` outcome was drawn as a ragdoll lie-down while the sim's health bar was nearly full (attribution: 20 light swings, ?rules=v1 = 0 falls, everything else 4-6). Flip `default` back to m4 only when Physics' row fix (killAs stagger, knockdown only on a heavy swing, pool tracking the sim's health) is proven by a 20-light-swing zero-falls clip plus one heavy that drops him. The text below describes M4 when it is on. Dom 2026-10-26: the physics package's M4 hit/cut rules evaluator (@frankendom/physics createEvaluator / evaluateHit, docs/API.md 'Rules evaluator', docs/M4-CALIBRATION.md) drives the opponent's ragdoll. PRESENTATION ONLY like data/physics.json: the 60 Hz sim (duel.ts) and Gate 0 never see it and nothing it does goes back into the sim. src/fight/rules-eval.ts reads every number and name here. ON by default (Dom 2026-10-27, 'all in the game, playable, M3456'; and 'everything on the main URL, no flags', which lifted the earlier hold): `default` names the ruleset a page with no ?rules= (or an unknown value) gets. `?<query>=<v1>` (?rules=v1) is the way back to V1's rules (every landed blow the same stagger); `?rules=m4` is M4 explicitly. The rest of the page is unchanged under either. WHAT IT DOES ON: each sim Hit whose target is the opponent (the ragdoll exists only for him; a missile or a guarded blow is not a hit on his body) becomes one evaluateHit: `weapons` the attacker's V3 weapon -> the package's nearest weapon row (`rule`; `blunt` = a crushing weapon, evaluated as kind blunt) -- the package has only gm_gladius, gm_katana, gm_claymore, gm_dagger, gm_rapier, gm_battleaxe (and two with no length), so a longsword is the katana (0.97 m), a cleaver the battleaxe (1.04 m, longer than a cleaver), a trident and an estoc the rapier (1.15 m, slash 0.34, so they stab), a knife the dagger, and the hammers, maul, scythe, reaper and staff the battleaxe (blunt for the hammers, maul and staff); the kind is stab for a thrust (move-rows isStabMove), blunt for a `blunt` weapon, else slash. `swing` heavy for the moves in `heavyMoves` or the overhead heavy and its directional heavies (isHeavyMove), a CHARGED blow too; else light. `counterHit` is the sim's own counter / stop-hit flag on the Hit event. `zone` is the Hit's location (head, torso, legs; `legs` on `legSide`). `armour` per opponent (the Minotaur wears none today: tier `none`). `t` is the Hit's tick / `tickHz` (sim seconds). SPEED (the FALLBACK: see TUNING below for the per-hit speed): the sim has no hand speed, so without a measured one every blow is the package's TYPICAL LIGHT swing (rules.swing.hand_speed_ref_m_s.<handSpeedRef> = light_p50, 6.25 m/s; light_p90 = 9.74 is the full-speed swing its calibration table uses, and with it a longsword (the katana row, lever 2.72) cuts or kills on any torso or head blow, so a bare Minotaur would fall to every hit; flip this one row to see it) multiplied by the weapon's lever inside the evaluator; a heavy takes the SAME light reference with swing heavy (heavy_mult 1.92 stands for the charge: feeding the heavy animation's faster speed too would count it twice, Physics Dev's flag). WHAT IT DRIVES: outcome hit / stick -> the ragdoll's stagger with the blow's impulse scaled by strength (`impulseAt`: the package's strength rung at which the impulse is physics.json hit.impulse; clamped to `impulseClamp`); knockdown -> rd.knockdown(cause) for the evaluator's fall + down seconds, the bones following the ragdoll, then a get-up blend of `getUpS`; cut -> the blow staggers as a hit and the unit is queued (rules.cuts): it comes off the CORPSE when the sim kills him (ragdoll.ts cutUnit, physics.json cut; a living body cannot be carved yet), and under ?rules=m4 these evaluator cuts are the ONLY cut trigger (physics.json cut.onKill's head-zone rule, the corpse tap and the finisher's cut are off); kill -> the SIM decides death, never the evaluator: while the sim's opponent still lives the evaluator's kill is shown as a knockdown (`killAs`), counted in rules.deferredKills, and its fighter state is renewed (`renewOnKill`: the package's budgets are head 20 / torso 60, a bare Minotaur's head dies on one blow; V3's pools are the sim's); the sim's own Killed event is the only death, as before. A miss (below the speed gate or the hit rung) is no stagger. The evaluator state is one per page and renewed at the rematch. The last results, the totals and the cost are on globalThis.__v3Rules and window.__v3Fight.rules. TUNING (Dom's follow-up to M4, physics 1882ab1): (1) PER-HIT HAND SPEED: each frame the attacker's (the HERO's) animated hand bone (`handBone`, a data/rig.json bones key: hand_r) is sampled each frame RELATIVE TO ITS SHOULDER (`handFrom`, upperarm_r: no root motion or lunge, in the body's own metres, divided by the anchor's world scale); its speed is the displacement over the last `speedSpanS` seconds (0.05 s = 3 ticks, the package's own method in docs/M4-MEASURE.md, because V3's clips step at 20 fps and a one-frame difference reads 3x on the step frame) over that time, the fastest of the last `speedWindow` such speeds (first run read 22-25 m/s on a one-frame world-space step, 2.5x the package's p90) (the swing's peak is a frame or two before the contact the sim reports); a step over `snapOver` m/s is a pose snap, dropped; a stopped clock (stills) or no sample gives the `handSpeedRef` row as before. The animation speed goes in as the package's hand speed after two data rows: `speedScale` 0.5 (the package's speeds were measured on the Minotaur's clips: its light p50 is 6.25 m/s; the hero's light slash clips measure a median of 12.4 m/s relative to the shoulder (docs/stills/m4-tuning reports, 2.5x the package's p90), so the medians are matched: 6.25 / 12.4 = 0.50; an assumption of the same kind as the package's lever, to be re-measured on labelled clips) and, for a heavy swing, `heavyDivisor` 1 (the package divides a heavy clip by heavy_mult because ITS heavy clips ran 1.92x its lights; the hero's heavy clips measure at or below his lights (10.5 and 5.6 against 12.4), so there is no charge in the clip speed and the evaluator's heavy_mult x 1.92 is the only charge: not counted twice). The light-equivalent is clamped to `speedMin` (4.01 m/s: the package's hand p10, docs/M4-MEASURE.md) .. `speedMaxRef` (light_p90, the package's full-speed light swing); so a light and a heavy now differ per swing. (2) BUDGETS: the package's part budgets are a man's; `hp_scale` = his sim health (moves.ts, 190 for the pitborn) over a man's (rules.ts health, 150), and `budgets` sets single parts absolutely on top: head 40 (a non-cut heavy blow on the head is at most 31.6 damage at the cut rung 24.3 x zone 2.0 x 0.65, so no non-cut blow kills the bare Minotaur's head in one hit; a CUT removes the whole part budget by the package's rule, so a big enough head or torso blow still takes the part, as a kill the sim has not made: shown as a knockdown, deferred). test/rules-eval.test.mjs pins both.

cut.about: Strategy's ruling (b), 2026-10-27: under ?rules=m4 a KILLING blow goes to the sim's finisher rotation (ragdoll.ts: a finisher that is not the plain death sets mode 'skip'), which never asks the evaluator, so a head blow at the cut rung could not take the head. `precedence` says who wins for a killing blow in a zone (head, torso, legs): 'evaluator' = the evaluator judges that killing blow first and, if it cuts, the death is the plain ragdoll death carrying the evaluator's cut (the head leaves with the kill; the scene and the death cue play the plain death, ragdollFinisher(events)); 'finisher' (the default for a zone with no entry, and today's behaviour exactly) = the rotation plays as before. Only a HEAD-zone killing blow is 'evaluator'; torso and legs keep the rotation. A blow below the cut rung is not a cut, so it keeps the rotation whatever this says. Only ?rules=m4 reads it; the default fight is unchanged.
